cognitive_validation.rationale: The principle is presented as a coherent, systematic, immanent, nonsupernatural account rooted in social-Darwinist and sociological reasoning. It is internally consistent and explanatory in the mode of imaginary/social science, and Edith's inquiry into the evolution of law extends this rationalized logic.

novum_candidates.description: A quasi-Darwinian natural law framing the narrative: civilization renders life machine-like and static, and when 'the unexpected' erupts, the unfit perish while the fit survive by adjusting to strange grooves. This principle is offered by the narrator as the governing law of the storyworld and is embodied in Edith Nelson's mastery of the unexpected.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The narrator contrasts civilized, machine-like order and a 'prearranged pageant' of death against the raw accidental violence of the frontier, inviting the reader to see ordinary life defamiliarized. However this is thematic estrangement of the actual world rather than an estranging novum: the storyworld remains empirically our own, so it does not constitute a Suvinian world-altering difference.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The framing principle governs the whole narrative logic: the story is structured as a demonstration of the thesis stated in the opening, with the catastrophe and its aftermath functioning as the test of the fit individual. The transformed 'new world' after the killings and Edith's reasoned reconstruction of law all follow from this organizing idea.

novelty.rationale: The 'unexpected/survival of the fittest' framing is a naturalistic interpretive gloss on ordinary human experience, not a totalizing difference from the empirical world. Civilization becoming machine-like and the unfit perishing are rhetorical/philosophical assertions about the actual world (Klondike-era Alaska), not a world-altering estranging difference. Nothing in the storyworld deviates from the author's empirical norm; the setting, events (a murder, a frontier hanging) are mundane realism.

cognitive_validation.rationale: Edith's step-by-step deduction of the evolution of law is a coherent, immanent, nonsupernatural piece of social reasoning presented as genuine sociological inquiry, satisfying the cognitive dimension in the mode of social organization.

novum_candidates.description: Edith's derived social principle that law is nothing more than the collective judgment and will of any group of people, however small - scaled down until a group of two (Edith and Hans) constitutes a legitimate tribunal that tries, convicts, and executes Dennin.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The improvised two-person tribunal defamiliarizes the concept of law by pushing it to a minimal limit, but this is an intellectual/thematic estrangement within a realistic frontier setting, not a novum that transforms the story universe.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The law-as-group-will reasoning drives the resolution (the trial and hanging), giving it substantial narrative weight, but it functions as a resolution mechanism subordinate to the overarching 'unexpected/fitness' frame rather than governing the whole narrative logic.

novelty.rationale: This is a sociological insight and an improvised application of frontier miners'-meeting custom, not a totalizing difference from the empirical world. Extralegal frontier justice and majority-will law are historically real; no aspect of the story universe is altered from our own by this reasoning.
